RECONSTRUCTION REVIEW
Reconstruction review

Start with an unfurnished reconstructed apartment and its fixed fixtures. Applying replaces the current shell, furniture, systems, finishes and renovation options. Original source attachments are kept without room assignments. Undo restores the previous apartment. Printed: plan identifies section 4, apartment type 13, total 41.3 m2. Table room numbers: 1 entrance hall 2.3; 2 living room 16.8; 3 bedroom 14.2; 4 bathroom 4.6; 5 balcony 3.4 m2. Measured: scale 56.86 pixels/m from living 327 pixels/5.750 m, bedroom 290 pixels/5.100 m and bathroom 145 pixels/2.550 m. Living height 190 pixels/3.350 m provides an independent vertical check. Origin is the upper-left nominal interior datum (456,393) on the source image. Measured: traced wall bands, stepped bathroom outline, three structural-column intrusions, entrance cupboard recess and two balcony doors. Thin cyan dimension lines are not walls. Hall/living boundary is an assumed zoning line across continuous floor, with no partition. Measured: bathroom shower at upper left, toilet below it, cyan-cross washing-machine footprint by the north column and basin at north wall. Kitchen hob, sink and refrigerator are drawn along the north wall. Gray crossed boxes beside and below the bathroom are service shafts, represented as solid wall masses. Assumed: no photographs were supplied. All floor and paint colours, ceiling height 2.6 m, door heights, window sills 0.35 m and heads 2.55 m, cabinet heights and materials are placeholders, not photo measurements. Assumed: cyan crossed balcony fixture is an outdoor service/AC unit; its function is not labelled. Upper kitchen cabinets and built-in cupboard heights are inferred. No separate oven or radiator is identifiable, so none is invented. Derived: printed room areas sum to 41.3 m2. Dimensioned bounding rectangles differ from usable room areas because of recesses, shafts, columns and open hall zoning; polygons follow the drawing rather than forcing the table areas. Measured: exterior balcony edge between its solid end piers is a railing, not a full-height wall. Door/window openings span their raster gaps.

RECONSTRUCTION REVIEW
Reconstruction review

Start with an unfurnished reconstructed apartment and its fixed fixtures. Applying replaces the current shell, furniture, systems, finishes and renovation options. Original source attachments are kept without room assignments. Undo restores the previous apartment. Printed: apartment type 13, section 4, total 41.3 m2. Schedule: hall 2.3, living 16.8, bedroom 14.2, bathroom 4.6, balcony 3.4 m2. Measured: scale approximately 57 pixels/metre, cross-checked against living width 5750 mm (328 px), bedroom width 5100 mm (290 px), bedroom depth 2750 mm (157 px), bathroom width 2550 mm (145 px), and living depth 3350 mm (191 px). Coordinates use plan-right +x and plan-down +z. Printed: bathroom depth 2100 mm; balcony width 1000 mm and length 3150 mm. These and the schedule are transcribed independently of polygon areas. Derived: hall and living/kitchen have an open shared boundary. Their division is inferred from room number positions; no wall has been added on this division. Hall polygon includes the recessed cupboard floor, which can explain an area difference from the schedule. Measured: structural columns, the kitchen service shaft, the bathroom southwest shaft and the stepped exterior have been retained as solid wall footprints, excluding their interiors from room floors. Measured: both balcony door gaps, the bedroom door, bathroom door and exterior entrance are represented over the full drawn gap. East balcony facade is open railing, not a full-height wall. Assumed: no photographs were supplied. All floor, wall and fixture colours, 2.6 m ceiling, 2.05–2.2 m door heights, window sill 0.25 m and window height 2.25 m are provisional and not photograph measurements. Measured: plan shows shower, toilet, basin, kitchen hob/sink/appliance, built-in cupboards and a cyan balcony utility symbol. Assumed: the latter is an outdoor utility appliance; the upper-left bathroom rectangle is a storage unit. Kitchen upper cabinets, oven, fixture heights and cabinet depths are inferred; no radiators or washing machine are identifiable. Derived: printed room areas are not substituted for traced geometry. Balcony schedule area 3.4 m2 differs from its approximately 1.0 by 3.15 m dimension rectangle; bedroom and bathroom also include local recesses or structural exclusions. Verification limitation: standalone output folder has no project test/build command or supplied geometry checker. JSON structure, opening bounds and reference integrity checked locally; downstream application validation remains separate. Verification limitation: top-down raster rendering could not run because the Python imaging library is unavailable. Geometry was compared directly to the cropped plan.
